**Refined prompt:** Design (not implement) a `comment.author` relation for this NestJS/TypeORM RealWorld API — entity change, write path, read path, and the ownership check it unblocks — answering as someone bound by this repo's conventions (RO envelope, nested bodies, controller→service→repository, spec conformance) and by LESSONS.md, with every claim cited to file:line and gaps stated. · Assumptions: you skipped the scoping questions, so I'm defaulting to **staged** (Stage 1 ships alone) and **nullable column, no backfill**.

---

# Design: `author` on comments

Unblocks the second CURRENT_FOCUS.md item (`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` — "the comment case needs a `comment.author` relation that does not exist yet").

## Stage 1 — relation + ownership check (shippable alone)

### 1.1 Entity

`src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15` has three columns and no link to `user` (`schema.md:50-57`). Add:

```ts
@ManyToOne(type => UserEntity, { nullable: true })
author: UserEntity;
```

- **`nullable: true` is forced.** `synchronize: true` with no migration files (`workspace.md:22`, `schema.md:6-8`) means a `NOT NULL` column added against a table with existing rows fails at boot.
- **No inverse side on `UserEntity`.** `ArticleEntity.author` has one (`article.entity.ts:37` ↔ `user.entity.ts:37-38`) because `create()` pushes through it (`article.service.ts:181-182`). Nothing needs "all comments by user" — a `UserEntity.comments` `@OneToMany` would be dead weight.
- **Do not add `eager: true`.** See §3 — it's a password leak, not a convenience.

Result: `comment` gains an `authorId` FK, alongside `id`/`body`/`articleId`.

### 1.2 Write path

The route is already guarded (`article.module.ts:28`), so `req.user` is set and `@User('id')` resolves — but the handler doesn't ask for it today (`article.controller.ts:77`).

```ts
// article.controller.ts
async createComment(@User('id') userId: number, @Param('slug') slug,
                    @Body('comment') commentData: CreateCommentDto)
```

`userId` goes first, matching `create()` (`article.controller.ts:52`), `favorite()` (`:94`), `unFavorite()` (`:102`). Service signature `(userId, slug, data)` matches `favorite(id, slug)` (`article.service.ts:131`).

In `addComment()` (`article.service.ts:101-112`), load the user and set `comment.author` alongside the existing `comment.body = commentData.body`. Keep copying `body` **by name** — do not `Object.assign(comment, commentData)` (LESSONS.md #112; `POST /:slug/comments` has no validation pipe, `workspace.md:82-84`).

> Incidental: lines 107-110 both `push` onto `article.comments` and save the article. With the FK on the owning side, `commentRepository.save(comment)` is sufficient. Optional cleanup, not required by this design.

### 1.3 The comparing line

`deleteComment()` (`article.service.ts:114-129`) has no ownership check, and `auth.md:60` records *why*: "comments have no author to compare against anyway." That excuse expires here.

```ts
const comment = await this.commentRepository.findOne(id, { relations: ['author', 'article'] });
if (!comment || comment.article.slug !== slug) throw new HttpException('Comment not found.', 404);
if (!comment.author || comment.author.id !== userId) {
  throw new HttpException('You are not the author of this comment.', HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
}
```

Per LESSONS.md #6, the line to name is `comment.author.id !== userId`. Three things that make it work rather than silently pass:

- **`relations: ['author']` is mandatory.** `author` is not eager, so without it the property is `undefined`, not `null` — the exact trap in LESSONS.md ("A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`", which burned `favorite()` at `article.service.ts:135`).
- **`comment.article.slug !== slug`** — today the `:slug` param is only used to load the article and scan its comment list (`:115-118`); the comment id is never checked to belong to that article. Without this, `DELETE /articles/any-slug/comments/42` works.
- **Null author ⇒ 403.** Legacy comments become undeletable through the API. That is the accepted cost of "nullable, no backfill"; if it bites, backfill `authorId` by hand and revisit.

This makes the `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` at `article.controller.ts:83` true for the first time (`auth.md:63-65`).

Controller takes `@User('id') userId` — route is guarded at `article.module.ts:29`.

### 1.4 Module

**No change.** `article.module.ts:13` already registers `[ArticleEntity, Comment, UserEntity, FollowsEntity]`, and both comment routes are already in the middleware list (`:28-29`).

---

## 🔴 The load-bearing risk: do not make `author` eager

`ArticleEntity.comments` is `{eager: true}` (`article.entity.ts:40`). `ArticleRO.article` is typed as the **raw `ArticleEntity`** (`article.interface.ts:25`), so whatever loads gets serialized.

If `comment.author` were eager, every `articleRepository.findOne` — `findOne` (`:97`), `addComment` (`:102`), `deleteComment` (`:115`), `favorite` (`:132`), `unFavorite` (`:148`), `findComments` (`:166`) — would return a full `UserEntity` per comment, including the argon2 `password` hash (`user.entity.ts:25-26`). `ProfileService.findOne()` does `delete user.password` (`profile.service.ts:26`) precisely because this is the known hazard.

So: load `author` explicitly where needed, and map to a profile shape at the boundary (§2.1).

**Pre-existing leak, same family, worth a separate ticket:** `findAll()` does `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')` (`article.service.ts:30`) and returns the entities — `GET /api/articles` already serves every author's password hash today.

**What I did not verify:** I'm relying on TypeORM 0.2.x honouring `eager` in `find*` but *not* in `createQueryBuilder` — which is why `findAll`/`findFeed` (`:28`, `:75`) don't load comments while `findOne` does. I did not run this against a DB. It decides only how *wide* the leak above is, not the design; confirm before relying on it.

---

## Stage 2 — spec-conformant comment payload

Independent of Stage 1; do it with the `favorited`/`favoritesCount` pass already in flight (`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`).

### 2.1 Shapes

`CommentsRO`'s element interface is `{ body: string }` (`article.interface.ts:3-5`) — no `id`, no author, no timestamps. The spec's comment is `{id, createdAt, updatedAt, body, author: Profile}`.

```ts
import { ProfileData } from '../profile/profile.interface';

export interface CommentData {
  id: number; createdAt: Date; updatedAt: Date; body: string; author: ProfileData;
}
export interface CommentRO  { comment: CommentData; }
export interface CommentsRO { comments: CommentData[]; }
```

Reuse `ProfileData` (`profile.interface.ts:1-6`) rather than inventing a shape — it's exactly what `findProfile()` already emits (`profile.service.ts:35-39`). A private `toCommentData(comment, followingIds)` mapper in `ArticleService` is the only place a `UserEntity` becomes a profile, and the only place `password` gets dropped.

### 2.2 Timestamps

`Comment` has none (`schema.md:50-56`). Add `created`/`updated` + `@BeforeUpdate()` mirroring `article.entity.ts:23-32`, and rename to `createdAt`/`updatedAt` **in the mapper, not the DB** — that's the rule `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9` sets for the article fields, and `workspace.md:91-93` documents the split.

### 2.3 `findComments` and `following`

Query `commentRepository` directly with `relations: ['author']` rather than going through the article's eager list (`article.service.ts:166-167`) — it doesn't depend on eager behaviour and it's one query.

`following` needs the caller, and `GET /articles/:slug/comments` is public (`auth.md:45-47`; absent from `article.module.ts:23-31`). Use `@User('id') userId` — the decorator returns `undefined` with no token (`user.decorator.ts:18`), the optional-identity case, guarded as `if (userId)` exactly like `profile.service.ts:43-45`.

Compute it in one shot: `followsRepository.find({followerId: userId})` → `Set` of `followingId` → look up per comment. `FollowsEntity` is already injected (`article.service.ts:22-23`). Do **not** call `findProfile()` per comment — that's an N+1.

**Blocking dependency:** `@User()` calls `jwt.verify` with nothing catching it (`user.decorator.ts:15`). Making this public route read identity newly exposes it to LESSONS.md #79 — an expired token turns `GET /articles/:slug/comments` from a working public request into a **500**. Fix the `jwt.verify` wrap first, or don't add `following` here.

### 2.4 Two response shapes that are wrong regardless

Flagging, not folding in — each is its own decision:

- `POST /:slug/comments` returns `ArticleRO` (`article.service.ts:101,111`); the spec returns `{comment: {...}}`. This is LESSONS.md #57 territory — a RealWorld frontend reads `response.comment`.
- `DELETE /:slug/comments/:id` returns `{article}` (`:124,126`); the spec returns an empty 200.

---

## Blast radius

| File | Stage 1 | Stage 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `comment.entity.ts` | `+author` | `+created/updated`, `@BeforeUpdate` |
| `article.service.ts` | `addComment`, `deleteComment` | `findComments`, mapper |
| `article.controller.ts` | `@User('id')` ×2 | `@User('id')` on `findComments` |
| `article.interface.ts` | — | `CommentData`, `CommentRO`, real `CommentsRO` |
| `article.module.ts` | none | none |
| `schema.md`, `auth.md:60` | update | update |

Not read: `prisma/` (`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24` — not the production path), `tag/`, `app.module.ts`. No code changed; this is design only.

Want me to implement Stage 1?
